主要内容: In 2017, the Hang Seng Index outperformed other major Asian indexes, rising more than 35 percent year-to-date. This was driven by strong gains from major blue chips, including Tencent, which reached all-time highs. The index also crossed the 30,000 mark for the first time since 2007. South Korea's Kospi index also performed well, rising 21.63 percent year-to-date, supported by global economic recovery and improved export performance. The KSE 100 Index, Pakistan's star performer last year, slumped this year due to political uncertainty. The global economic recovery and improved risk appetite contributed to the overall positive performance of Asian markets, with MSCI's broad index of shares in Asia Pacific excluding Japan up more than 34 percent year-to-date. Vietnam emerged as a standout among emerging markets, with the Vietnam Stock Index rising 46.9% year-to-date, driven by investor confidence in the country's growing economy. Despite being classified as a frontier market by MSCI, Vietnam is working to improve accessibility for foreign investors and has taken steps to privatize state-owned firms, such as the sale of a majority stake in Sabeco to Thai Beverage. Analysts believe this could help reduce Vietnam's national debt and attract foreign direct investment. Meanwhile, Pakistan's performance declined, with the KSE 100 Index falling over 15% due to political uncertainty. Global economic growth is expected to continue, but concerns remain about the impact of policy normalization after years of easy money. OCBC Bank highlighted the shift from geopolitical risks to 'gray rhinos' as a major theme for 2018, emphasizing the potential for volatility from China's debt management efforts.
